Synopsis:
    The article covers near-term FX outlook for four Sub-Saharan African currencies. The Ghanaian cedi and Ugandan shilling face continued depreciation pressure — the cedi from corporate FX demand and reduced Bank of Ghana auction supply, the shilling from energy import-driven dollar demand linked to Middle East tensions. The Kenyan shilling is expected to hold steady. The Zambian kwacha is seen consolidating, supported by elevated copper prices offsetting import demand.
